question: Why did 'Rock Around the Clock' sell little in 1954 and top the charts in 1955?
answer: The record barely sold at first. A year later it played over the opening of the film 'Blackboard Jungle', and teenagers who heard it in cinemas made it a number one. Thompson's point: a hit needs distribution as much as quality; the same song can fail or triumph depending on who hears it.
move: Quality alone rarely makes a hit; ask who got to hear it.
simply: A great song nobody hears is like a great joke told in an empty room. Put it in a film everyone sees, and suddenly it's a hit.
why: For your own work too: reaching the right audience can matter as much as making the thing better.

book.title: Hit Makers
book.author: Derek Thompson
